chapter_theme: The kinds of body (உடலிற் பஞ்சபேதம்): the soul lives in a gross body of the seven bodily elements, a subtle body of eight tattvas and finer bodies still; the subtle body carries it from birth to birth to taste its deeds, while for the knower the body becomes Siva, so the body is not to be despised.
structure_note: The body as nested bags (2122), the subtle eightfold body (2123, 2124), the gross body (2125), the bodies and their measure (2126 to 2130), the subtle body's passage between births (2131 to 2134), the body according to the kind of soul (2135, 2136), and a defence of the body (2137, 2138).

2122.reading: There is one bag of a body with many wares in it; there is one bag of maya and another bag besides; when the thief who stood inside the body-bag goes out, the maya-bag turns to earth: such is the bewilderment.
2122.nuance: The three bags are traditionally the gross, subtle and causal bodies, and the thief the soul, which slips out unseen. The verse names only the body-bag and the maya-bag clearly.

2123.reading: Of the body the Father fashioned in two parts, the pure subtle one, when spoken of, is sound, touch, form, taste, smell, intellect, mind and ego: the eightfold body.
2123.nuance: புரியட்டகம் (puryashtaka) is the subtle body of eight in Siddhanta: the five subtle elements with buddhi, manas and ahankara. The two parts are the gross and the subtle body.

2124.reading: Within the eight, the five senses and the three bound instruments arise; as the clinging bond becomes awareness, the one with the eye in his forehead binds and unbinds.
2124.nuance: This verse nearly repeats 473. The eight are the eight of 2123; the three கரணம் are traditionally mind, intellect and ego. Siva both binds the soul in the body and releases it.

2125.reading: Chyle, blood, flesh, skin, fat, bone with its grease, marrow and the semen that spreads: this is the perishing adjunct, and but for its form, the body may be called one.
2125.nuance: The list is the seven or more bodily elements (dhatus) of the gross body. உபாதி (adjunct) marks the gross body as something laid over the soul. The last line is unclear: perhaps the body is one thing, differing only in form.

2126.reading: Who knows the greatness of the feet? Who knows where they stood? Who knows the sixty-eight bodies? Who knows what became the guard of the feet?
2126.nuance: அறுபத்தெட்டு ஆக்கை (sixty-eight bodies) has no settled meaning; it may be a count of bodily parts or of kinds of body. அடி may be the Lord's feet or the base of the body.

2127.reading: In the body built to eight spans, in eye, foot and body and in the hands that flow, the sixty-eight bodies join, and by that union the body becomes a body of itself.
2127.nuance: எண்சாண் (eight spans) is the traditional measure of the human body, each by its own hand. புண்கால் and the sixty-eight are obscure, and the reading is tentative.

2128.reading: The soul that is life to the body and the four inner faculties subsides into the Supreme; Brahman, showing the measure that stands in each pot, is stilled and gone: who knows this?
2128.nuance: கடந்தொறும் (in each pot) recalls the Vedanta image of one space in many pots, the one Brahman in many bodies. நாலு is read as the four inner instruments. How the lines fit together is unclear.

2129.reading: When the six ends join with the middle, the clear three sixes hold firm; the eighteen kalas spoken of join together, and the life counts the welling body as its own body.
2129.nuance: ஆறு அந்தம் may be the six ends (the antas of Saiva doctrine) or 'the six as end'; மூவாறு and the eighteen kalas are counts whose content the verse does not give.

2130.reading: The body whose gross face abounds in flesh, the body in which the subtle sits in what is unreal, the body that shows the finest as if in the hand: all are bodies held within the Lord's feet.
2130.nuance: தூலம், சூக்கம், துல்லியம் name gross, subtle and finest bodies. மெய் and பொய் pun on body and truth, falsehood; the sense of the middle lines is uncertain.

2131.reading: As a fierce galloping horse sets down one foot and lifts another, the body can go far and near; leaving one coat of flesh and putting on another there, it fits itself to whoever it becomes.
2131.nuance: The subject is read as the subtle body, which passes from one gross body to the next. The coat image (போர்வை) is the gross body worn and shed.

2132.reading: Like a snake leaving its slough, it may go, and by Hara's grace it goes to the place it must go and eats the two fruits.
2132.nuance: The two fruits are good and bad deeds' results, as tradition reads them. Line 2 (நனாவில் கானா மறந்து) seems to speak of waking and dream but is obscure and may be corrupt.

2133.reading: Having eaten what is in hell and heaven, the subtle body leaves and goes on as the cause; with its old deeds following, like a yogi who enters another's body, it takes up a body and meets birth and death.
2133.nuance: பரகாய யோகி is the yogi with the power to enter another body, one of the attainments in the siddhi chapter; here it is a simile for the subtle body taking a new birth.

2134.reading: One who has borne the Supreme and become Him changes what has come and reaches the highest; other souls go to the place their deeds bring them and suffer, entering sky and earth.
2134.nuance: தான் அவன் ஆகிய (he who became He) states union plainly. ஆனவை மாற்றி may mean undoing the bodies and deeds that came to him.

2135.reading: For the knower, the body, once established, becomes Siva; for the knower the body itself becomes That; for the yogi it is bindu and nada; for the silent sage the body is release in which the three voids are destroyed.
2135.nuance: மேனி in line 3 may be another class of seeker or simply 'body'; முப்பாழ் (the three voids) is a technical term, traditionally taken as maya, the soul's state and the void beyond, but this is not fixed.

2136.reading: For the vijnanakalas the body is anava itself; for those of the next kind, maya, it is said, is the body; for those without knowledge, karma becomes the body; those of true knowledge take on a body of Siva.
2136.nuance: The classes follow 494: விஞ்ஞானர் (bound by anava alone), எஞ்ஞானர் (taken as the pralayakalas), அஞ்ஞானர் (the sakalas, bound by all three malas). Each one's 'body' is the impurity that holds it.

2137.reading: See the dull ones who, calling the body filth, do not value it and hold some other place to be sacred; if one seeks and holds to this body as good, one grasps this whole cosmos in the strong body.
2137.nuance: மலம் may be filth or the soul's impurity; தலம் என்று வேறு தரித்தமை is read as taking another place (a shrine, or another body) as holy. The last line rests on the body as microcosm (அண்டம்).

2138.reading: Speech, mind and the rest, in good utterance, play gently within the Stainless; the others, the ear, sound and the rest and the mind as well, those who have gently held them see Him, hungering.
2138.nuance: The verse is obscure and the reading a guess. It seems to set the faculties at play in the Lord against the senses gently held in check; முகத்தார் பசித்தே is unclear.

links.note: Both make the body a bag left behind when its occupant goes: in 167 the dancer leaves the leather bag, so what crows do to it no longer matters; in 2122 the thief leaves and the maya-bag turns to earth.
2124 repeats 473 almost word for word; in the chapter on conception it describes the forming embryo, here the subtle body of eight.

Both list the body's stuffs, fat, blood, bone, flesh, skin. The Naladiyar asks which of these is the beloved, to cure desire; Tirumular names them as the gross adjunct beneath the subtle bodies, without disgust.
494 names the classes of soul (விஞ்ஞானர், எஞ்ஞானர், மெய்ஞ்ஞானர்) by the malas they have left; 2136 gives each its body: anava, maya, karma, or Siva.
725 says Tirumular once thought the body a flaw, then found the Lord's temple within it and now tends it; 2137 calls those who dismiss the body as filth dull.

The Naladiyar says the great saw the body's foulness and abandoned it; Tirumular calls those who disregard the body as filth dull and finds the cosmos in it. The conflict holds if மலம் in 2137 is read as bodily filth, as here.

source_issues: 2124 nearly repeats 473 (473 has எட்டினுள், ஆய்விடும், பாச உணர்வென்னுங் காயப்பை, கட்டி அவிழ்த்திடுங்).
2132 line 2 (மாக நனாவில் கானாமறந் தல்லது) is obscure; கானா may be for கனா (dream).
2138 is obscure throughout and may be corrupt.
2136: எஞ்ஞானத் தோர்க்கு is an unusual name for the pralayakalas, matching 494's எஞ்ஞானர்.
